title: The Girl in His Phone
disclosure: Original fictional Reddit-style story. AI-generated voice. Background footage is illustrative.

parts.text: My fiancé told me not to open one message. So I did.

We were eleven days away from our wedding. Three years together. A venue booked. A ring I still caught myself staring at. Then his phone lit up with a woman's name. Nora. The message said, I sent the last thousand. Please don't disappear again.

He grabbed the phone and called her an obsessive ex. He said blocking her would only make things worse. I wanted to believe him. But that night, another message appeared on our shared tablet. It was a photo of me. A selfie I had taken that morning.

I found Nora's number in the conversation and sent one question. How do you know my fiancé? She replied with a screenshot. My face. My name. Our holiday pictures. Then she wrote, Your fiancé? I've been dating you for eight months.

My fiancé wasn't dating her as himself. He was pretending to be me. Every missed video call had an excuse. Every photo came from our life. He'd told her I was trapped with a controlling boyfriend and needed money to leave. She thought she was helping the woman in the pictures escape.

Then Nora asked about the ring in my selfie. She had sent twelve hundred dollars two days before he proposed. He'd told her it was an emergency apartment deposit. I still had the jeweler's receipt. Same amount. Same date. The woman I thought was stealing my fiancé had paid for my engagement ring.

We compared everything before confronting him. The messages. The transfers. The dates. His first question wasn't whether we were okay. It was whether we'd told anyone. I cancelled the wedding. Nora reported the account and the payments. And I changed every password he knew.

I'd spent days hating a woman who thought she was rescuing me. In the end, she actually did. So what would you do? Tell every wedding guest exactly what happened, or cancel quietly? Tell me why in the comments.
